questions.skill: Derive and use the formula for the area of a sector
questions.standard_level: Geometry. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Geometry, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.response: write the answer and show the required work
questions.prompt: Derive a formula for the area of a sector with central angle θ (in degrees) in a circle of radius r. Then rewrite it for θ in radians.
questions.prompt_markup: Derive a formula for the area of a sector with central angle θ (in degrees) in a circle of radius r. Then rewrite it for θ in radians.
questions.correct_answer: A = (θ/360)πr² for degrees; A = ½r²θ for radians.
questions.required_method: Use the fraction of the whole circle that the sector is, times the circle's area.
questions.grading_note: Any valid proof (paragraph, two-column, or flow). Essential: the sector is θ/360 of the circle (central angles split the area in proportion); area = (θ/360)πr²; with θ radians, the fraction is θ/(2π), so A = (θ/(2π))πr² = ½r²θ.

questions.prompt: Derive the formula A = ½rs for the area of a sector in terms of its radius r and arc length s. Then use it for a sector with r = 8 and s = 5.
questions.prompt_markup: Derive the formula A = ½rs for the area of a sector in terms of its radius r and arc length s. Then use it for a sector with r = 8 and s = 5.
questions.required_method: Use the fraction s/(2πr) of the circumference, which is the same fraction of the area.
questions.grading_note: Any valid proof (paragraph, two-column, or flow). Essential: the sector is s/(2πr) of the circle (arc length and area are in the same proportion to the whole circle); A = (s/(2πr)) · πr² = ½rs; ½ · 8 · 5 = 20.
